notes: CBSA's sort-code service (GETSCODE, LINKed by the web front end's GetSortCode API with the GETSCODE copybook's 6-byte COMMAREA): MOVE LITERAL-SORTCODE (the SORTCODE copybook's 77 SORTCODE PIC 9(6) VALUE 987654, renamed by COPY ... REPLACING) TO SORTCODE OF DFHCOMMAREA (PIC X(6)), then EXEC CICS RETURN. The transaction is CJSA, the CICS Liberty JVM server's default for a web request (the corpus defines none for these programs; the program never reads EIBTRNID). One path, no condition: the scenarios differ only in what the caller leaves in the COMMAREA. The COMMAREA is described by the GETSCODE copybook's group GETSORTCODEOperation (6 bytes, the whole of DFHCOMMAREA): the program's own DFHCOMMAREA cannot be laid out from GETSCODE.cbl, whose WORKING-STORAGE COPY SORTCODE REPLACING the harness's layout reader refuses. scenarios.name: blank-commarea
scenarios.why: the COMMAREA arrives as spaces: SORTCODE becomes '987654' (an unsigned numeric DISPLAY to alphanumeric MOVE: the digits as they are)

scenarios.name: caller-sortcode-replaced
scenarios.why: the caller's sort code is overwritten by the program's own

scenarios.name: letters-replaced
scenarios.why: non-digits from the caller: all six bytes replaced

scenarios.name: no-commarea
scenarios.why: the caller passes no COMMAREA (EIBCALEN 0, no DFHCOMMAREA): the program still MOVEs the sort code, never testing EIBCALEN

scenarios.name: eibcalen-zero
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN 0 with the COMMAREA record present (X23): the MOVE reaches past the bytes the caller passed

scenarios.name: eibcalen-short
scenarios.why: the caller passed 3 of the 6 bytes: the MOVE writes all 6, past EIBCALEN

scenarios.name: longer-sortcode
scenarios.why: the caller's sort code is 8 characters for the 6-byte SORTCODE: the stated value overruns the field and the MOVE replaces it whole

scenarios.name: eibcalen-full
scenarios.why: EIBCALEN equals the record (6 bytes, X23): the COMMAREA is stated exact, so the area is cut to the 6 bytes the caller passed and the MOVE fits exactly

scenarios.name: dto-entry-blank-commarea
scenarios.why: as blank-commarea, but the port gets the typed DTO alone (no link-area bytes): the typed entry (in_) and the DTO it gives back (fill_) are what is compared (#5863)

scenarios.name: dto-entry-caller-sortcode
scenarios.why: as caller-sortcode-replaced, through the typed DTO alone: the caller's 6 digits read by in_ and replaced whole (#5863)

scenarios.name: dto-entry-letters
scenarios.why: as letters-replaced, through the typed DTO alone: non-digit caller data read by in_ and replaced whole (#5863)
